newsitem.title: EGYPT: France says time ripe for Europe role in Mideast.
newsitem.headline: France says time ripe for Europe role in Mideast.

text.p: A French envoy to the Middle East said on Sunday that the time had come for Europe to take its place alongside the United States at the centre of peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians.

But France does not have a specific initiative to offer and it will avoid entering into competition with Washington, traditionally the dominant mediator in Arab-Israeli talks, Bertrand Dufourcq told a news conference in Cairo.
Dufourcq, an envoy from President Jacques Chirac and secretary general of the foreign ministry, is on a regional tour to prepare for Chirac's own tour, which starts on Saturday.
The French visits are in parallel with a revival in European Union interest in the peace negotiations, which have ground to a stalemate since the right came to power in Israel in June.
Dufourcq met Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa on Saturday and President Hosni Mubarak on Sunday. He will be in Israel on Monday and the Palestinian territories on Tuesday.
"We think that the moment has absolutely come where Europe must play a role... With our knowledge, our experience and our contacts we can help," he said.
"We want to be present and with the various parties to see in what way we can make a contribution... When negotiations meet certain problems, one can perhaps make some suggestions," he added.

The envoy insisted that Israel must respect the agreements it has already signed with the Palestinians, starting with the agreement on the West Bank town of Hebron, but Europe and France would not otherwise take sides in any disagreements.

"One should not imagine a kind of coalition, one side against the other, that's not our view of things. We are neither on one side nor the other, we are on the side of peace and the search for a peace that must be fair and lasting," he said.

"We want to work in full coordination with the Americans," he added. "It's not a question of entering into sterile competition. We must couple our efforts. It is in the interests of the negotiations that Europe be present."
But Dufourcq implicitly acknowledged that Israel and the United States had reservations about giving Europe a role.
"We have to succeed in convincing our friends and our partners that we are not people who obstruct or upset the negotiations. On the contrary...we can help," he said.
Mubarak said on Saturday that any European role must be coordinated with the U.S. role, which he called fundamental.
"We do not want conflicts, in which the loser would be the cause (of peace)," he said.
